answer.rationale: The binding constraints are structural, not preference-based: the incumbent has refused to reopen price (so memory_c4's renegotiation lever and memory_c6's multi-year volume lever are both closed this cycle), the contract does not auto-renew in 14 days (so memory_c5's defer-and-drift path does not apply to a critical, expiring primary supply), and memory_c3's add-second-source play does not by itself secure primary supply past expiry. That leaves switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor as the only direction that both meets the 18% mandate and keeps volume covered past day 85. I want memory_c2 verified because it is the single memory carrying the entire decision: everything rests on the claim that the low-cost vendor onboarded quickly and invoiced accurately. That record is consolidated and its source is archived, so I am reading a summary of a summary. The specific things I need from the original: which component and which volume tier, whether the line had buffer at the time, and whether 'quick onboarding' meant qualified-and-ramped or merely first-article-accepted. Memory_c2 reads as a clean win, and a clean-win summary is exactly where an unrecorded caveat is most likely to have been compressed out. The material difference from memory_c2's context is that the line is now at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. A cutover that was low-risk against slack is not low-risk against none, so I am not treating memory_c2's success as transferable at full scale. Hence standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout: qualify and ramp the low-cost vendor on a phased volume share with the incumbent's final deliveries covering the transition window, rather than a single-date full cutover. This captures most of the mandated savings while keeping a fallback path if first-article or ramp slips. Downstream risk I am flagging explicitly: if this succeeds it will be consolidated as a second 'switching to low-cost vendor works' record stacked on memory_c2, and the next agent will inherit two mutually reinforcing summaries with the 94%-no-buffer condition and the phased structure stripped out. It should be recorded that the mandate and the hard expiry forced this, that price renegotiation was unavailable rather than untried, and that the ramp was phased specifically because there was no buffer. Residual uncertainty I cannot close within one verification: whether the quoted price holds at our full volume, and whether the low-cost vendor has capacity headroom for the sole-source position memory_c3 warns against leaving unhedged. Adding a second source remains the right next-cycle move once primary supply is secured.
